court: High Court of Judicature at Madras
trial_court: Subordinate Judge, Dharapuram, H.M.O.P. No.45 of 2008
facts_of_case: Petitioner filed for divorce under Section 13 of Hindu Marriages Act. Respondent was served but did not appear. Exparte decree granted in favour of petitioner. Respondent then sought to set aside the decree citing delay.

legal_principles.principle: Sufficient cause must be shown for allowing the petition filed under Section 5 of the Limitation Act.
legal_principles.held: Sufficient cause is a question of fact and the Court has to exercise its discretion in the varied and special circumstances in the case at hand. There cannot be a strait-jacket formula of universal application.

legal_principles.principle: The court has no jurisdiction to set aside an exparte decree under Order IX Rule 13 CPC.
legal_principles.held: The matter does not fall within four corners of Order 9 Rule 13 CPC and the Court has no jurisdiction to set aside the exparte decree.
applicable_acts_sections: Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 — Order IX Rule 13

legal_principles.principle: The court's discretion in condoning delay is guided by rules and principles of law.
legal_principles.held: Condonation of delay is a judicial discretion by the Trial Court guided by rules and principles of law...
cited_cases: Kasipalayam Town Panchayat vs Arumugam, (2005) 2 CTC 362

outcome.final_order: Court condoned the delay and set aside the exparte decree.

use_for_drafting: appealing court orders in family law cases
